item.title: BYOD Policy for Solar Subcontractors Recording Customers
item.description: Right now, on a subbie’s phone somewhere in your network, there’s a video of one of your customers standing in their kitchen. The switchboard might be in the background, or the metre, or the customer talking through what they were promised at the sale. It sits in the camera roll next to the subbie’s kids’ footy photos. It has probably already gone up to their personal cloud account, and quite possibly into a WhatsApp group with two other installers.

item.title: How to Find and Keep Solar Subbies Who Are Worth Keeping
item.description: Every installer who uses subbies has a story about the one who cost them a customer. Not because the job was unsafe and not because the licence was dodgy. The paperwork was clean. The system worked. The subbie just left a mess on the roof gutter, parked across the neighbour’s drive, didn’t sweep up the offcuts, and treated the customer’s home like a worksite instead of someone’s house. The customer never rang to complain. They just quietly decided they would not be recommending you to anyone.
